newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar finishes lower, seen weak.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar finishes lower, seen weak.

text.p: The strength of the American currency against major currencies in Asia trading pulled the Taiwan dollar lower at Wednesday's close and dealers said they expected the local unit to move further lower.
"Some exporters were selling U.S. dollars today but buying was much bigger as the U.S. dollar continues to surge in overseas markets," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The local rate finished at T$27.515, off an intra-day high of T$27.525, compared with Tuesday's T$27.485 close. Turnover through dealers totalled a hectic US$465.5 million.
"Seeing the strong U.S. dollar against the Japanese yen, many banks started to cover their short positions on the U.S. dollar," the dealer said.
"They should continue buying as the U.S. dollar uptrend is very strong," the dealers said, adding that she did not expect the central bank to intervene.
The central bank has pledged repeatedly to fully respect market forces and said recent foreign exchange volatility was both "useful and helpful" for the market.
The local unit could test T$27.55 on Thursday, dealers said. -- Joyce Liu (2-5080815)
